findings.title: Denial cache key does not include identity type, allowing cross-identity poisoning
findings.body: permDenialKey is built only from namespace, raw UserUID, action, name and parent. Anonymous subjects (anonymous:0) and the render service (render:0) both parse to UserUID "0", and user/service-account subjects can also share UID strings. A denial cached for anonymous:0 on dashboards:read/dash1 is therefore returned for render:0 on the same resource, even though getRendererPermissions would grant renderers read access to all dashboards/folders. The same collision can deny a user or service account based on another identity type's denial. The identity type (checkReq.IdentityType) must be part of the denial key.

findings.title: Denial cache blocks newly granted permissions and defeats the fresh-DB recheck
findings.body: Check returns immediately on a permDenialCache hit and never re-queries the DB, while the entry written at line 154 lives for shortCacheTTL (30s) and is never invalidated when permissions change or when permCache is refreshed (e.g. by a List or another Check that fetches fresh permissions). A user who checks a dashboard/folder before its permission grant is visible, then creates/receives access to it, remains denied for up to 30s despite this PR's stated goal of letting creators immediately access newly created resources via a DB requery on cached-permission misses.

findings.title: Denial cache key uses ambiguous underscore delimiters for name and parent
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates userUID, action, name and parent with '_' separators, but dashboard/folder UIDs legitimately contain underscores. Distinct tuples collide: (name="c_d", parent="e") and (name="c", parent="d_e") produce the identical key, as do userUIDs containing underscores combined with shifted name/parent segments. A denial for one resource can therefore incorrectly deny a different resource in a different folder for 30s. Fields should be encoded unambiguously (e.g. length-prefixed or escaped/hashed).

findings.title: Every cached-permission miss for a distinct resource triggers a full DB permission fetch
findings.body: When cached permissions do not allow the check, Check unconditionally calls getIdentityPermissions, and this PR removed the permCache lookups inside getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions, so that call always queries basic role, teams and the permission store (singleflight only dedupes concurrent identical keys, not sequential calls). Checking many distinct resources the user legitimately cannot access (e.g. listing/probing dashboards) causes one full DB fetch per resource until each individual resource's denial entry is populated, largely negating permCache for negative checks and risking DB load under denied-request traffic.
